right_upper_lobe.name: Right Upper Lobe
right_upper_lobe.description: The top lobe of the right lung.
facts: The right lung has three lobes: upper, middle and lower.
Separated from the middle lobe by the horizontal fissure.
Its tip (apex) rises slightly above the collarbone.

right_middle_lobe.name: Right Middle Lobe
right_middle_lobe.description: The smallest lobe of the right lung, at the front between the upper and lower lobes.
facts: Only the right lung has a middle lobe.
Bounded by the horizontal fissure above and the oblique fissure below.
Lies next to the heart.

right_lower_lobe.name: Right Lower Lobe
right_lower_lobe.description: The bottom lobe of the right lung, resting on the diaphragm.
facts: Separated from the other right lobes by the oblique fissure.
Rests on the dome of the diaphragm, which sits higher on the right because of the liver.
A common place for inhaled objects to end up, because the right main bronchus is more vertical.

left_upper_lobe.name: Left Upper Lobe
left_upper_lobe.description: The top lobe of the left lung.
facts: The left lung has only two lobes, leaving room for the heart.
Has a notch for the heart called the cardiac notch.
Has a tongue-like part called the lingula, which matches the right middle lobe.

left_lower_lobe.name: Left Lower Lobe
left_lower_lobe.description: The bottom lobe of the left lung, resting on the diaphragm.
facts: Separated from the upper lobe by the oblique fissure.
Rests on the left dome of the diaphragm.

trachea.name: Trachea (Windpipe)
trachea.description: The tube that carries air from the larynx down into the chest, where it splits into the two main bronchi.
facts: About 10-12 cm long and 2 cm wide in adults.
Kept open by about 16-20 C-shaped rings of cartilage.
Lined with cilia and mucus that trap dust and move it up towards the throat.
Splits into the left and right main bronchi at the carina.

bronchi.name: Bronchi
bronchi.description: The branching airways that carry air from the trachea into each lung.
facts: The right main bronchus is shorter, wider and more vertical than the left.
They divide again and again into smaller bronchi and then bronchioles.
The smallest airways end in alveoli, tiny air sacs where oxygen passes into the blood.
